## Concepts and practice

These concepts are covered in Quiz 1 (next week's tutorial). Textbook: Chapters 4 and 11.

### Concept list

| Concept | In one sentence |
|---|---|
| Narrative review | A summary of the literature without a predefined, reproducible method for finding and selecting studies. |
| Systematic review | A review that answers a focused question with a predefined, reproducible method to find, select, appraise and synthesise all relevant studies. |
| Meta-analysis | The statistical pooling of the results of the studies included in a systematic review into one summary estimate. |
| PECO / PICO | The elements of a focused review question: Population, Exposure (or Intervention), Comparison, Outcome. |
| Eligibility criteria | The predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria a study must meet to be included in the review. |
| Search strategy | The combination of databases, search terms and Boolean operators used to find all potentially relevant studies. |
| Screening | Selecting studies in two steps: first on title and abstract, then on full text. |
| PRISMA 2020 | The reporting guideline for systematic reviews, including the flow diagram of identified, screened and included studies. |
| Cohort study | An observational study that follows exposed and unexposed people over time and compares how often the outcome occurs. |
| Case-control study | An observational study that compares the past exposure of people with the outcome (cases) to people without it (controls). |
| Cross-sectional study | An observational study that measures exposure and outcome at the same moment. |
| Observational versus experimental | In an observational study the researcher does not assign the exposure; in an experiment (such as a randomised controlled trial) the researcher does. |
| Hierarchy of evidence | The ranking of study designs by how well they support causal conclusions. |

### Practice questions

**1.** A researcher selects 200 children with autism and 400 children without autism and asks their parents which vaccines the child received. Which study design is this, and why?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Answer
A case-control study: participants are selected on the outcome (autism or not), and past exposure (vaccination) is then compared between cases and controls.
:::

**2.** Formulate the review question of this module in PECO format.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Answer
P: children; E: thimerosal-containing vaccines; C: thimerosal-free vaccines (or lower exposure); O: autism spectrum disorder.
:::

**3.** Why is a meta-analysis not always possible, even after a good systematic review?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Answer
Because the included studies may be too different (in population, exposure, outcome or design) or may not report the data needed to pool their results. The review then stays a systematic review with a narrative synthesis.
:::
